Surah "Al-Haqqah" (The Inevitable Reality)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

﴿Al-Haqqah﴾: the Hour that is certain to occur, whose coming is established, which is surely coming, there being no doubt about it. It is derived from "ḥaqqa, yaḥiqqu" (ḥaqqa, with the vowel i in the imperfect), meaning: it became obligatory (wajaba).

﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ — "ما" is the subject and "الحاقة" is the predicate, and the two together form the predicate of "الحاقة" (the Inevitable Reality). The original structure is "الحاقة ما هي؟!" ("The Inevitable Reality — what is it?!" / "What thing is it?!"), in order to magnify its matter and glorify its terror; that is, its due is that one ask about it, because of its greatness. The apparent noun has been placed in the position of the pronoun, for the sake of increasing the awe.

**And what will make you know** [the meaning is], and what informs you,

**﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾** [al-Haqqah: 2]. That is, you have no knowledge of its true nature or the extent of its greatness, for it is so great and so severe that the understanding of created beings cannot reach it. "**Wa ma**" (وَما): the word **ma** is in the nominative case by **al-ibtida'** (the inception, i.e. it is the subject of a nominal sentence). "**Adraka**" (أدْراكَ) is the predicate (khabar). The clause that follows it is in the accusative position, because it is the **second object** (maf'ul thani) of **adra** (أدرى).

Surah 69, verse 4: ﴿Thamud and 'Ad denied the Striking Calamity.﴾ That is, (they denied) the Inevitable Reality (al-Haqqah). The Striking Calamity (al-Qari'ah) was placed in the position of al-Haqqah, because it is among the names of the Resurrection (al-qiyamah). It was called by this name because it strikes people (taqra'u al-nas) with terrors and dreadful events (bil-af'zi'a wal-ahwal). When He mentioned it and magnified its significance, He followed the mention of it with the mention of those who denied it and what befell them because of their denial, as a reminder to the people of Makkah and a warning to them about the consequence of their denial.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 5:

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Tāghiyah﴾, that is, by the catastrophe that exceeded all bounds in severity. Its identity has been disputed. It has been said: it is the quake (al-rajfah). It has been said: it is the cry (al-sayhah). It has been said: al-ṭāghiyah is a verbal noun (maṣdar), like "al-ʿāfiyah," meaning: by their transgression (bi-ṭughyānihim). But this does not fit His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 6:

﴿And as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a wind⁠﻿﻿﻿﻿—﻿—﻿—﻿—﻿—﻿—﻿—

Let me correct that and give the full translation cleanly:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 6:

﴿And as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a wind﴾, that is, by the dabūr (the west wind), because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I was given victory by the ṣabā (the east wind), and ʿĀd were destroyed by the dabūr."

﴿ṣarṣarin﴾, violently loud in sound, from "al-ṣirrah," meaning the cry; or cold, from "al-ṣirr," as if it were the one in which cold was repeated and abounded, so that it burns with the intensity of its cold;

﴿ʿātiyah﴾, of intense force, or it rebelled against its keepers, so they could not control it, by the permission of Allah, in anger at the enemies of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 7:

﴿Sakhkharahā﴾ (He subjected it), sallaṭahā (He gave it power over them),

﴿ʿalayhim sabʿa layālin wa-thamāniyata ayyām﴾ (against them for seven nights and eight days). The beginning of the punishment was on Wednesday, at the end of the month, until the next Wednesday,

﴿ḥusūman﴾ (continuously), i.e., consecutive, without interruption. It is the plural of ḥāsim (one who cuts off), like shuhūd (witnesses) from shāhid, as a comparison to their succession by the succession of the action of the ḥusām (the cauterizing iron) in repeating the cauterization on the disease, time after time, until it is eradicated (yanḥasima). It is also permissible for it to be a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning: it eradicates (taḥsimu) eradication (ḥusūman), in the sense of "it uproots with complete uprooting" (yastaʾṣilu istiʾṣālan),

﴿fa-tarā﴾ (so you see), O addressee,

﴿al-qawma fīhā﴾ (the people in it), in its directions, or in the nights and days,

﴿ṣarʿā﴾ (fallen), a circumstantial state (ḥāl), the plural of ṣarīʿ (fallen),

﴿kaʾannahum﴾ (as if they were), another circumstantial state,

﴿aʿjāzu﴾ (trunks), i.e., the roots (uṣūl),

﴿nakhlin﴾ (of palm trees), the plural of nakhla (palm tree),

﴿khāwiyatin﴾ (hollow), fallen, or decayed (bāliya).
﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ That is, a surviving soul, or some survival, as in *"al-ṭāghiyah"* (the tyrannical one), meaning *"al-ṭughyān"* (the transgression, or rebellion).

And Pharaoh came, and those before him (﴿وَجاءَ فِرْعَوْنُ ومَن قَبْلَهُ﴾), meaning the nations that preceded him. As for "wa-man qablahu," it is read by Basri and Ali (as "wa-man qiblahu"), meaning: those who were with him of his followers.

﴿وَالْمُؤْتَفِكَاتُ﴾ (And the overturned cities): the towns of the people of Lot. They were "ui'tufikat," meaning they were turned upside down with their inhabitants.

﴿بِالْخَاطِئَةِ﴾ (with the sinful deed): with the error, or with the act, or with deeds that involve great error.

﴿So they disobeyed﴾, that is, the people of Lot,

﴿the messenger of their Lord﴾, namely Lot,

﴿so He seized them with a severe seizing﴾ (p-530): intense, increasing in severity, just as their abominations had increased in ugliness.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 11:

﴿Indeed, when the water rose beyond its measure﴾, it rose at the time of the Flood above the highest mountain in the world by fifteen cubits,

﴿We carried you﴾, meaning: your forefathers,

﴿in the sailing ship﴾, that is, in the ship of Noah, upon him be peace.

﴿So that We may make it﴾, that is, the deed, namely the rescue of the believers and the drowning of the disbelievers,

﴿for you a reminder﴾, a lesson and an admonition,

﴿and retain it﴾, and preserve it,

﴿an ear﴾, with a ḍamm (the short vowel u) on the dhāल, which is the reading of everyone other than Nafiʿ,

﴿that retains﴾, preserving what it hears. Qatada said: "It is an ear that understood from God and benefited from what it heard."
﴿And when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast﴾. It is the first blast, at which people die, and the second, at which they are raised.

["And the earth and the mountains are lifted up"], they are raised from their places.

["Then they are crushed with one crushing"], they are pounded and broken, meaning: some of them are struck against others, until they are pulverized and return to being a heap of sand, poured out, and scattered dust.

﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: that is, ﴿فَحِينَئِذٍ﴾ (then, at that time).

﴿وَقَعَتِ الواقِعَةُ﴾: the Inevitable Event (al-waqi'a) occurred, the descending calamity (al-nazila) descended, and it is the Resurrection (al-qiyama).

The response (jawab) of "إذا" (idhā, the temporal conditional particle) is "وَقَعَتْ" (waqa'at, "occurred"), and "يَوْمَئِذٍ" (yawma'idhin, "on that day") is a substitute (badal) for "إذا".

And the sky will be split open, [so] it will be opened into gates.

﴿So on that Day it will be frail﴾: slack, its strength gone, after having been firmly made.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 17:**

﴿And the angels﴾: al-malak is a collective noun (jins), meaning in the sense of a plural, and it is more general than al-mala'ika (the angels).

﴿Upon its sides﴾: that is, its edges. Its singular is "raja" (rajā'), a maqsur (shortened-form) noun, because when it splits open, and it is the dwelling place of the angels, they take refuge at its extremities.

﴿And above them, on that day, eight will bear the throne of your Lord﴾: above the angels who are upon its sides.

﴿Eight﴾: of them. Today it is borne by four, and four more will be added on the Day of Resurrection. It is related from al-Dahhak: "eight rows." It has also been said: "eight kinds."

﴿On that Day you will be presented﴾: for the reckoning and the questioning. He likened this to a ruler reviewing his army in order to learn their condition.

﴿Not a thing about you will be concealed﴾: no secret (سَرِيرَة) and no state that was hidden in the world. It is read with the letter ي (bi-l-yāʾ, "with yāʾ") by the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim.

In a ḥadīth: "People will be presented on the Day of Resurrection in three presentations. As for the first two, there will be disputing and excuses. As for the third, then the pages will fly, and the successful one will take his book in his right hand, and the one who is lost will take his book in his left hand." (ﷺ)

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 19:

﴿As for﴾ is an elaboration of the presentation (al-'ardh),

﴿he who is given his record in his right hand, so he will say﴾, out of joy at it, because of the good things he sees in it; it is addressed to his group (jama'ah),

﴿Here, take﴾: "hā'um" is a noun functioning as a verb (ism li-l-fi'l, i.e. a noun acting as a verb), meaning: take,

﴿Read my record!﴾ Its underlying form is: "Hā'um kitābī, iqra'ū kitābiyah" (Here, take my record; read my record!). The first object was deleted because the second indicates it. The governing element (al-'amil) in "kitābiyah" is "iqra'ū" according to the Basrans, because they give precedence to the nearer governor. The ha' (al-ha' al-sakt, the pausal ha') in "kitābiyah," "hisābiyah," "māliyah," and "sulṭāniyah" is for pausal purposes (li-l-saktah); its proper place is to be retained in pause and dropped in continuous speech (al-wasl), and it is preferred to favor pausing, to preserve it, since it is written in the Mushaf.

﴿Inni ẓanantu﴾ means "I knew" (ʿalimtu). The word ﴿ẓanantu﴾ (I supposed) is used in the sense of knowledge (ʿilm), because the predominant supposition (al-ẓann al-ghālib) takes the place of knowledge in customary matters and in legal rulings. Also, what is grasped through ijtihad (independent reasoning) is rarely free of whisperings (waswās) and passing thoughts (khawāṭir), and these lead to suppositions (ẓunūn). So it is permissible to apply the word ẓann to them, since they are not free of it.

﴿Inni mulāqin ḥisābiyah﴾ means: "Indeed I am meeting my reckoning," that is, "I am witnessing (muʿāyan) my reckoning."

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 21:

﴿So he will be in a pleasant life﴾, possessing contentment, with which its possessor is pleased, like "*lābin*" (ﻻﺑﻦ), meaning "one who possesses milk."
Qur'an 69:22: ﴿In a lofty garden﴾, lofty in its place, or lofty in its ranks, or lofty in its buildings and palaces. And this is a predicate following a predicate.

"Its clusters are near at hand" (qutufuha daniyah). Its fruits are close to the one who desires them; the one standing, the one sitting, and the one reclining can all reach them, and it is said to them:

Eat and drink with pleasure, [enjoying] eating and drinking with pleasure, with nothing disagreeable or harmful in them; or, "you have been made to feel pleasure" (hanī'tum hanī'an), in the verbal-noun form (ʿalā al-maṣdar).

for what you sent forward, that is, for what you had put forward of righteous deeds.

in the days that have passed, that is, the bygone days of the worldly life. And it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "It refers to those who fasted," meaning: eat and drink in exchange for what you refrained from eating and drinking for the sake of Allah.
(p-532) ﴿But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: "Would that I had not been given my record!"﴾ — because of the disgraces he sees recorded in it.
﴿And I did not know what my account is﴾. That is: "Oh, would that I had not known what my account is!"

"Oh, would that it had been the end!" — would that the death I died had been the decisive one,

﴿Would that it had been the decisive end﴾ — that is, the one that cuts off my affair, so that I would not have been raised after it and would not have met what I am meeting.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿What has my wealth availed me?﴾ (69:28). Meaning: it did not benefit me what I amassed in the world. "Ma" is a negation, and the object is omitted, i.e., "anything."

Note on the translation: the Arabic has "ما أغنى عني مالية" in the text, which the instruction's markers enclose; the rendering above follows the Qur'anic meaning.

"﴿My authority has perished from me﴾: my kingship and my dominion over the people. And I remained poor and humbled." It is also reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "My proof has been lost to me," meaning: my argument by which I used to argue in the world has been nullified. Then Allah (Exalted) says to the guardians of Hellfire:
"Take him and shackle him" (Qur'an 69:30). That is, gather his two hands to his neck.

Verse 31: ﴿Then into the Blazing Fire, cast him.﴾ Meaning: make him enter (the Fire). That is, "Then do not cast him into anything but the Blazing Fire, which is the great Fire." Or "al-Jahim" is in the accusative governed by a verb implied and explained by "ṣallūhu" (cast him).

Then (put him) in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, [that is,] its length; seventy cubits, by the cubit of the angel, according to Ibn Jurayj. And it has been said: "No one knows its measure except Allah."

"Then thread him" means: insert him (into it). The purpose of placing the chain before the threading is like the purpose of placing the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim) before the burning (al-tasliyah).

"Indeed he" — an explanatory clause (ta'lil). It is as if it were said: "Why is he punished with this severe punishment?" And the answer is given with "Indeed he..."

﴿Indeed he used not to believe in Allah, the Mighty.﴾

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 34:**

﴿And does not urge the feeding of the needy﴾: that is, does not urge the giving of food to the needy. This indicates that he did not believe in the Resurrection, for people do not seek a reward from the needy for what they feed them. They feed them only for the sake of Allah and in hope of reward in the Hereafter. So when he did not believe in the Resurrection, he had nothing to move him to feed them. That is, despite his disbelief, he would not encourage others to feed the needy. There is also a strong proof here of the gravity of the sin of withholding from the needy, for He joined it to disbelief, made it a sign of disbelief, and a companion to it. He mentioned "urging" rather than the act itself, so that it would be understood that if one who merely fails to urge is in this position, then one who fails to act is more deserving of it. It is related from Abu al-Darda' that he used to urge his wife to make more broth for the sake of the needy, and he would say: "We removed half of the chain by faith, so we will remove the other half by this." (p-533) These verses clearly show that believers will all be shown mercy, while disbelievers will not be shown mercy, for He divided creation into two categories. He made one category the people of the right hand, and described them only by faith, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account﴾ [al-Haqqah: 20]. And He made the other category the people of the left hand, and described them by disbelief, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, he did not believe in Allah, the Mighty﴾ [al-Haqqah: 33]. It is also possible that a believer who is punished is punished only before his book is given to him in his right hand.

Translation:

﴿So today he has no friend here﴾, a close friend who would repel (the punishment) from him, and whose heart would burn for him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 36:

﴿Nor any food except from ghislin﴾, the washing-water of the people of the Fire. "Ghislin" is of the pattern "fislin", derived from "al-ghasl" (washing), and the nun is an added letter. What is meant here is what flows from their bodies of pus and blood.
﴿None eats it except the sinners (al-khati'un)﴾, the disbelievers, the people of sins. And "khati'a al-rajulu" means the man deliberately committed a sin.
﴿Fa-lā uqsimu bimā tubṣirūn﴾ — "So I swear by what you see," from among the bodies, the earth, and the sky.
﴿And by what you do not see﴾, of the angels and the spirits. The summary is that He swore by all things.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, it﴾ means: indeed, the Qur'an,

﴿is the word of a noble Messenger﴾ means: Muhammad (ﷺ), or Jibril (peace be upon him), meaning: by his speech, and he recites it in the manner of a message from Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 41:

﴿And it is not the word of a poet﴾, as you claim,

﴿little is it that you believe﴾

"Nor is it the word of a soothsayer, as you claim," (﴿وَلا بِقَوْلِ كاهِنٍ﴾)

"little do you remember" (﴿قَلِيلا ما تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾). It is read with the ya' (yā', i.e. "yadhakkarūna" with the third-person form) in both places by Makki, Shami, Ya'qub and Sahl, and with the dhal lightened (tukhaffafu al-dhāl, i.e. "tadhakkarūna" becomes "tadhakkarūna" with a single dhāl, read as the lightened form) by the Kufans except Abu Bakr. The paucity (qillah, "little") here carries the sense of non-existence (ʿadam): it is said, "This is a land that hardly produces anything" (qallama tunbitu), meaning it produces nothing at all. The meaning is: you do not believe, and you do not remember at all.

﴿Tanzil﴾ (a revelation): it is a revelation, explained: because it is the word of a Messenger to whom it was sent down,

﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾
(p-534) ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings﴾, and if he had claimed against Us something that We did not say.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 45:

﴿Lam seized him by the right hand﴾, we would have slain him in cold blood, as kings do with one who lies against them, hastening to them with wrath and vengeance. Thus He depicted the slaying in cold blood in its own form, so that it would be more terrifying, which is that one takes his hand and his neck is struck. The right hand was specified because the slayer, when he wants to bring the blow down upon the back of the neck, takes hold with the left; and when he wants to bring it upon the neck, and to strike him with the sword across the face, which is more severe for the one being depicted because of his looking at the sword, he takes hold with his right hand. The meaning of "﴿Lam seized him by the right hand﴾" is: we would have seized him by his right hand, and so on.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 69, verse 46:

﴿Then We would have cut from him the aorta (al-watin)﴾. "We would have cut his watin," and the watin is the niyat of the heart (the sinews or vessels attached to the heart); when it is severed, its owner dies.

﴿So none of you﴾: the address is to mankind, or to the Muslims.

﴿from anyone﴾: "مِن" is extra (زائِدَةٌ).

﴿from Him﴾: from killing Muhammad.

He used the plural ﴿preventers﴾ (حاجِزِينَ), although it is an attribute of "أحَدٍ" (aḥad, "anyone"), because it carries the sense of a group (jamā'ah). An example of this is His, Exalted is He, saying: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285].

"And indeed it" — that is, and indeed the Qur'an,

"is a reminder" — an admonition,

"for the God-fearing."

And indeed it (wa-innahu): and indeed the Qur'an,

﴿and indeed it is a cause of regret for the disbelievers﴾, that is, for those who denied it, when they see the reward of those who affirmed it.

**Verse 51:** ﴿And indeed it﴾, that is, the Qur'an,

﴿is the truth of certainty﴾, that is, the certainty of sight (ʿayn al-yaqīn), and pure certainty (maḥḍ al-yaqīn).
﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾. So glorify God by mentioning His name "al-ʿAẓīm" (the Mighty), which is His saying: "Subhan Allah" (Glory be to God).
